To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of tumor cell contamination in adjacent normal breast tissue samples, rather than genetic field effects, is the most likely explanation for the high local recurrence rates following conservative breast surgery.

we found evidence of tumor cell contamination in 14/32 HER2-positive breast tumor-normal tissue pairs, and that these tumor cells were identified by histologic and IHC examination as small, HER2-overexpressing tumor cell foci scattered within the normal adjacent tissue.

HER2-amplification is associated with the presence of HER2-positive tumor cell foci in normal breast tissue adjacent to the primary tumor, and that these HER2-positive tumor cells are the likely cause of local recurrences after breast conserving surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new and potentially important clinical problem that may be relevant in other tumor sites, and may have important implications for the design of clinical trials and for the clinical management of patients.
a better understanding of the biology of breast cancer and the mechanisms underlying the development of local recurrences following breast conserving therapy.
the molecular mechanisms of breast cancer progression and metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field cancerization hypothesis is not proven by these studies.
the presence of tumor cells, even if small, in normal breast tissue is a risk factor for local recurrence.
HER2-amplification in breast tumors is not associated with genomic field cancerization, but that it may be associated with the presence of tumor cell clusters in the adjacent normal tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HER2-amplification in breast tumors is not a field effect, but is a result of the tumor itself, and that HER2-positive breast cancer cells can be present as isolated clusters of tumor cells in the normal breast tissue adjacent to the tumor, which can be detected by genomic methods.

we have demonstrated that the presence of HER2 gene amplification in normal breast tissue adjacent to HER-positive breast tumors is not due to field cancerization effects, but is rather the consequence of tumor cell contamination.

we found that in HER2-positive breast cancers with a high risk of local recurrence after breast conservation therapy, the risk is not due to genetic field cancerization, but rather to occult foci of tumor cells extending beyond the invasive margin of the tumor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genomic analyses of normal adjacent tissue from breast cancers may be misleading and that caution is warranted in interpreting such results.
genomic aberrations in normal adjacent mammary tissues are likely due to tumor cell contamination rather to field cancerization.
the histologic normality of the adjacent tissue samples used to extract DNA does not guarantee the genomic normalcy or absence of tumor cells within these samples.
